entities.summary:
ABC-CLIO is an American academic and reference publisher — founded in 1953 by Eric Boehm as the American Bibliographical Center-CLIO, Inc. — specializing in history, social studies, and humanities reference works for academic and educational institutions, and representing one of the most significant American academic publishers of encyclopedias, databases, and reference resources for libraries and educational institutions.

ABC-CLIO's publication portfolio includes major reference works widely used in American academic libraries: the America: History and Life database (comprehensive bibliographical index of articles on American and Canadian history), Historical Abstracts (similar index for world history), and numerous encyclopedias covering world history, political systems, and social issues. These databases have been standard research tools in academic libraries for decades, serving historians, students, and researchers with bibliographical access to scholarly literature.

The transition from print to digital reference publishing has been a major challenge and transformation for publishers like ABC-CLIO: their traditional business model of selling expensive multi-volume print encyclopedias to libraries has been disrupted by internet reference resources, but the databases like America: History and Life and Historical Abstracts have maintained value as curated scholarly bibliographic tools. ABC-CLIO (merged with Greenwood, Praeger, and Heinemann into ABC-CLIO's expanded portfolio) is now owned by private equity and navigates the challenging academic publishing market.
